questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Minsk?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Belarus is Minsk.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Belarus?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Belarus article.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Belarus?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Belarus on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Belarus article.

questions.proof: It is bordered by Russia, Ukraine, Poland, Lithuania and Latvia.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Belarus about 207,597 square kilometres; North Korea about 120,540 square kilometres; Serbia about 88,499 square kilometres; Switzerland about 41,291 square kilometres.

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Belarus on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Belarus on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
